analysis.investment_thesis: Avanti Feeds is a dominant shrimp feed player (~50% Indian market share) with a pristine balance sheet (D/E ≈ 0), but cyclical earnings and commodity-linked margins limit the durability of its moat. At 31.7x P/E, the market is pricing in perfection for a business that dropped net profit 38% in a single year (FY22).
key_strengths: Near-zero debt (INR 15 Cr borrowings vs INR 3,011 Cr equity) — fortress balance sheet with reserves compounding from 1,390 to 2,997 Cr in 5 years
Dominant market position in Indian shrimp feed with established brand trust among aqua farmers, creating meaningful switching costs
Revenue CAGR of 12.6% and net profit CAGR of 15% over 9 years with FY25 momentum (OCF 584 Cr, highest on record)
key_risks: Severe earnings cyclicality — net profit swung from 466 Cr (FY18) → 245 Cr (FY22) → 557 Cr (FY25); this is not the predictable earnings stream I require
Commodity input exposure (fishmeal, soya) compresses pricing power and squeezes margins, with operating margins already thin at 11.6%
Shrimp disease outbreaks (EMS, WSSV) and weather events can crater aqua farmer demand overnight — an uncontrollable external risk
red_flags: Other income surging to INR 166 Cr in FY25 (29% of net profit) — suggests core earnings quality is lower than reported; treasury gains are masking operating performance
Investing outflow of -485 Cr in FY25 with only INR 26 Cr cash on hand raises questions about capital deployment discipline
FY22 saw negative OCF (-212 Cr) and negative FCF (-267 Cr) despite a profitable P&L — working capital volatility in commodity businesses is a hidden risk
analysis.detailed_analysis:
Avanti Feeds runs a genuinely good business — it dominates India's shrimp feed industry, carries virtually no debt, and has compounded equity from INR 1,404 Cr to INR 3,011 Cr over five years. ROCE of 24% and ROE of 19.5% are respectable, and the FY25 recovery (net profit INR 557 Cr, OCF INR 584 Cr) is encouraging. But the 9-year earnings history tells a story I cannot ignore: profits nearly halved from FY18 to FY22 and OCF went sharply negative. When a business's fortunes hinge on shrimp disease cycles, monsoon patterns, and fishmeal spot prices, I struggle to predict earnings 10 years out — and that predictability is what I pay for.

At 31.7x trailing P/E and 21x EV/EBITDA, the stock prices in sustained compounding from a cyclical agri-commodity processor. The rapidly growing "other income" (INR 20 Cr in FY16 → INR 166 Cr in FY25, 26.5% CAGR) distorts the quality of reported earnings — strip it out and the core operating business is valued even more richly. I'd want to own this around 20–22x earnings with a clearer growth runway. A fair business at an expensive price is not my style.
